supreme-court-of-the-united-states: On December 4, 2025, the Supreme Court agreed to let Texas use a new Trump-backed congressional map in the 2026 midterm elections, with the conservative majority temporarily blocking a lower-court order that had found the map unlawful.[n] The map remains in play while the legal challenge continues, and the court's three liberal justices dissented.[n]
2026-redistricting-battle: The Supreme Court gave the Republican redistricting campaign a significant boost on December 4, 2025, agreeing to let Texas use its new Trump-backed congressional map in the midterms while litigation continues.[n] The order temporarily blocked a lower-court ruling that had found the map unlawful, over the dissent of the court's three liberal justices, and was described as a major development in a redistricting war among states to maximize Republican victories and maintain control of Congress.[n] Badlands host Jon Herold responded simply that readers should brace themselves because the midterms are coming.[n]
jon-herold: Commentary on the Texas map ruling

In the December 5, 2025 Badlands News Brief, Herold commented on the Supreme Court's decision permitting Texas to use its Trump-backed congressional map in the 2026 midterms, telling readers to brace themselves because the midterms are coming, and linking to his Daily Herold episode covering 'Bombergait, Signalgate and other gayts.'[n]
burning-bright: On MAGA influencer appeals to Trump

Writing in the December 5, 2025 Badlands News Brief, Burning Bright argued that observers should cast aside the messenger and focus on the message, contending that recent appeals to President Donald Trump from the MAGA influencer class ultimately aim to convince audiences that Trump is unfit for office.[n] He added that these figures 'told you who they were in 2022' and asked whether readers believed them.[n]
fbi: On Thursday, December 4, 2025, the FBI arrested a suspect in its nearly five-year investigation into who planted pipe bombs in Washington on the eve of the January 6, 2021 Capitol riot, according to a law enforcement official cited by the Associated Press.[n] The arrest marked the first time investigators had identified a suspect in a case that had remained unresolved for years and fueled widespread speculation; two senior law enforcement officials named Brian Cole as the man in custody, and a Justice Department news conference was scheduled later the same day.[n] The bureau had previously said both devices, discovered on the evening of January 5, 2021 near the Democratic and Republican national committee headquarters, were capable of causing deadly harm, though no one was injured.[n]
january-5-2021-pipe-bombs: Arrest of a suspect in December 2025

Nearly five years after the devices were discovered, the FBI arrested a suspect in the case on Thursday, December 4, 2025, according to a law enforcement official cited by the Associated Press.[n] Two senior law enforcement officials familiar with the matter identified the man in custody as Brian Cole, an FBI official confirmed the arrest had occurred that morning, and the Justice Department scheduled a news conference later in the day to formally announce it.[n] The arrest was the first public identification of a suspect in a case whose long non-resolution had fueled widespread speculation.[n] Badlands host Chris Paul rejected the official framing entirely, asking when people would accept that there were no 'pipe bombs' anywhere on January 6.[n]
chris-paul: In the December 5, 2025 Badlands News Brief, Chris Paul dismissed the FBI's pipe bomb arrest by asking when observers would accept that there were never any real pipe bombs on January 6.[n] He also mocked the Michigan absentee ballot ruling, quipping that 'a few more of these improvements and people will believe our fake elections are even more legitimate than before,' and joked about Halle Berry's appearance at the DealBook Summit.[n]
european-union: Der Spiegel reported in December 2025 that EU leaders harbored profound distrust of Washington's attempts to help end the Ukraine conflict, citing a transcript of a recent phone call among European leaders that the outlet had obtained.[n] The EU had outright rejected a US-drafted peace plan condition reportedly requiring Ukraine to cede parts of Donbass it still controls, insisting that Kiev should not give up any territory.[n]
emmanuel-macron: On Monday, December 1, 2025, Macron and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz held a phone call with Vladimir Zelensky and several other European leaders, including Finnish President Alexander Stubb and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, a day before Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner traveled to Moscow for talks with Vladimir Putin.[n] According to a transcript obtained by Der Spiegel, Macron said there was 'a possibility that the US will betray Ukraine on the issue of territory without clarity regarding security guarantees,' and warned that continued peace talks could pose a 'great danger' for Zelensky personally.[n]
friedrich-merz: Merz joined French President Emmanuel Macron on a December 2025 phone call with Vladimir Zelensky, Finnish President Alexander Stubb, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, and NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte, in which European leaders voiced deep distrust of the US-led effort to end the Ukraine conflict.[n] Merz was reported to share Macron's assessment that continued peace talks could pose a 'great danger' for Zelensky personally.[n] Badlands contributor GhostofBasedPatrickHenry addressed Merz directly, writing that Trump was going to betray him and his ilk 'because that is the morally righteous thing to do.'[n]
volodymyr-zelensky: European leaders' December 2025 call and the Yermak fallout

Zelensky took part in a December 2025 phone call with Emmanuel Macron, Friedrich Merz, Alexander Stubb, Ursula von der Leyen, and Mark Rutte in which the European participants voiced profound distrust of US peace diplomacy, and in which Macron warned that continued talks could pose a 'great danger' to Zelensky personally.[n] Separately, his former spokeswoman Yuliya Mendel said she feared for her life because of Andrey Yermak, Zelensky's long-time right-hand man, who resigned amid the Operation Midas corruption probe.[n]
alexander-stubb: Stubb participated in the December 2025 phone call convened by Emmanuel Macron and Friedrich Merz with Vladimir Zelensky and other European leaders about US-led Ukraine peace efforts.[n] According to Der Spiegel's account of the transcript, Stubb shared Macron's assessment that continued peace talks could pose a 'great danger' for Zelensky personally.[n]
ursula-von-der-leyen: Von der Leyen joined the December 2025 phone call held by Emmanuel Macron and Friedrich Merz with Vladimir Zelensky and other European leaders, held one day before US envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner traveled to Moscow for talks with Vladimir Putin.[n] Der Spiegel reported that the leaders on the call harbored profound distrust of Washington's attempts to end the Ukraine conflict.[n]
steve-witkoff: Witkoff, President Donald Trump's special envoy, traveled to Moscow with the president's son-in-law Jared Kushner in early December 2025 for talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin.[n] The visit came a day after European leaders held a phone call in which they expressed deep distrust of US peace diplomacy and warned that Washington might betray Ukraine on the question of territory.[n]
jared-kushner: Kushner accompanied special envoy Steve Witkoff to Moscow in early December 2025 for talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin on ending the Ukraine conflict.[n] European leaders, on a phone call the previous day, voiced fears that the United States would betray Ukraine on the territorial question without clarity on security guarantees.[n]
vladimir-putin: December 2025 Moscow talks with US envoys

Putin received US special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner in Moscow in early December 2025 for talks on ending the Ukraine conflict.[n] The meeting followed a call among European leaders who feared Washington would concede Ukrainian territory — reportedly including parts of Donbass still under Kiev's control — without firm security guarantees.[n]
mark-rutte: As NATO Secretary General, Rutte took part in the December 2025 phone call among European leaders about US-led Ukraine peace diplomacy, and according to Der Spiegel shared Emmanuel Macron's assessment that continued talks could pose a 'great danger' for Vladimir Zelensky personally.[n]
nato: December 2025 distrust of US Ukraine diplomacy

NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte joined a December 2025 phone call in which European leaders expressed profound distrust of Washington's attempts to end the Ukraine conflict and warned that the United States might betray Kiev over territory.[n] Badlands contributor GhostofBasedPatrickHenry welcomed the reported rift, writing that he views NATO and the European Union as the actual bad guys in the geopolitical conflict and hoping that both would collapse from financial mismanagement and public rebuke.[n]
pete-hegseth: Pentagon inspector general report on Signalgate

On December 4, 2025, the Pentagon inspector general released its long-awaited report on Hegseth's role in the Signalgate affair.[n] Investigators concluded that his use of the Signal messaging app to send updates about strikes in Yemen broke rules for handling sensitive information and risked putting troops in danger, even though he has the power to declassify such information as he sees fit.[n] Reporting on the release listed six takeaways: that he broke the rules, kept a very tight circle, offered up incomplete records, produced findings open to interpretation, failed to satisfy Democrats, and had changed his tune; analysts judged that nothing in it would doom Trump's most embattled Cabinet chief, though it could complicate his political future.[n]
pentagon: The Pentagon inspector general released its report on Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's use of the Signal messaging app on December 4, 2025, concluding that sending updates about strikes in Yemen over the platform broke rules for handling sensitive information and risked putting troops in danger.[n] The report found that Hegseth kept a very tight circle and had offered investigators incomplete records, while its overall significance was widely described as being in the eye of the beholder.[n]
katherine-maher: Badlands host CannCon pointed to Maher's role as chair of the Signal Foundation board — held alongside her position as chief executive of NPR, and following prior work with the National Democratic Institute, UNICEF, the World Bank, Access Now, the Atlantic Council, and the US State Department Foreign Policy Affairs Board — as grounds for questioning how and why senior US officials came to conduct sensitive discussions on Signal.[n]
npr: In December 2025 commentary on the Signalgate report, Badlands host CannCon highlighted that NPR chief executive Katherine Maher simultaneously chairs the board of the Signal Foundation, suggesting the overlap warranted scrutiny of the messaging platform's adoption by US officials.[n]
cisa: Badlands host CannCon raised the possibility that CISA had advised US officials to use the Signal messaging app during the Biden administration, roughly a month before President Donald Trump took office — a scenario he argued would recast the Signalgate controversy surrounding Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.[n]
signal: Signalgate and the December 2025 inspector general report

Signal was the platform at the center of the Signalgate affair, in which Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth transmitted updates about US strikes in Yemen; the Pentagon inspector general concluded in a December 4, 2025 report that this broke rules for handling sensitive information and risked putting troops in danger.[n] Commentators noted that the Signal Foundation's board is chaired by NPR chief executive Katherine Maher, and questioned whether CISA had encouraged officials to adopt the app during the Biden administration.[n]
jocelyn-benson: In December 2025 a Michigan judge rejected the position taken by Benson and Director of Elections Jonathan Brater that absentee ballots with mismatched identification numbers could be counted as 'challenged ballots' under decades-long administrative guidance.[n] The court held that election inspectors may count absentee ballots only when the stub and envelope numbers match, and that long-standing administrative practice cannot override the Legislature's 2024 strengthening of the matching requirement.[n]
republican-national-committee: The RNC, together with the Michigan Republican Party and Chesterfield Township Clerk Cindy Berry, won a December 2025 ruling from a Michigan judge over the state's handling of absentee ballots with mismatched identification numbers.[n] The plaintiffs argued that such ballots must be rejected while voters are given a chance to cure the defect, and the court agreed that there is no legal authority to tabulate a mismatched ballot under any category.[n]
jared-polis: Trump's December 2025 attack over Tina Peters

In a December 2025 Truth Social post, President Donald Trump called Polis the 'SLEAZEBAG Governor of Colorado' for refusing to release Tina Peters from jail, described Peters as an elderly cancer survivor unfairly convicted of 'what the Democrats do, cheating on Elections,' and closed with the demand 'FREE TINA!'[n] Trump also accused the governor of allowing his state 'to go to hell,' invoking the Tren de Aragua gang.[n] Badlands host Ashe in America said she took no issue with the characterization of the governor, calling it 'Golden Age Trump.'[n]
tina-peters: Trump's December 2025 clemency demand and Badlands commentary

President Donald Trump publicly demanded Peters' release in a December 2025 Truth Social post attacking Colorado Governor Jared Polis, saying she had served more than a year in jail with eight years to go, was a cancer survivor, and had been preserving election records she was obligated under federal law to protect.[n] Badlands host Ashe in America endorsed Trump's reading of the participants' intent but added precision: Peters was convicted of misrepresenting to the people she was investigating who was in her office, a response to arbitrary COVID-era rules issued by Secretary of State Jena Griswold about who could be present in county offices, and none of her charges or convictions were for cheating or meddling in elections.[n] Ashe argued the law was changed after the fact to criminalize what Peters did, called her ongoing treatment 'cruel, unusual, and unconstitutional,' and announced a marathon airing of a three-part series on the Peters story on her Rumble channel alongside coverage of the Peters-commissioned Mesa County reports with Colonel Shawn Smith on Why We Vote.[n]
jena-griswold: Obstruction claims and the DOJ records dispute

Badlands host Ashe in America wrote in December 2025 that Griswold, whose arbitrary COVID-era rules about who could enter county offices prompted the conduct for which Tina Peters was convicted, remained emboldened and was continuing to obstruct the Trump Justice Department on elections.[n] Griswold said in a statement that 'we will not comply with the Trump Department of Justice's request for Coloradans' sensitive voting information,' that the DOJ 'can take a hike' because it has no legal right to the information, and that Colorado 'will not help Donald Trump undermine our elections and hurt the American people.'[n] Ashe noted that Griswold had been obstructing inquiry since at least 2021, when she banned independent audits.[n]
paul-kagame: Kagame was hosted by President Donald Trump in Washington on December 4, 2025, alongside Democratic Republic of the Congo President Felix Tshisekedi, to sign deals aimed at stabilizing eastern Congo and attracting Western mining investment.[n] The two presidents were expected to pledge commitment to an economic integration compact agreed the previous month and to a US-brokered peace deal reached in June that remained unimplemented.[n] Badlands contributor GhostofBasedPatrickHenry characterized Kagame as a 'lapdog' of what he called the Israeli Diamond Cartel, which he argued had dispatched M23 rebels out of Rwanda to seize chokepoints and recover mineral control lost through Executive Order 13818.[n]
felix-tshisekedi: Tshisekedi joined Rwandan President Paul Kagame at the White House on December 4, 2025, where President Donald Trump brought the two leaders together to sign new deals aimed at stabilizing the war-scarred eastern Congo region and attracting Western mining investment.[n] Analysts said US diplomacy had paused escalation of the fighting but failed to resolve core issues, and days earlier the DRC military and M23 rebels had accused one another of violating the ceasefire.[n]
m23: Ceasefire violations and the December 2025 summit

The Rwanda-supported M23 rebel group seized the two largest cities in eastern Congo in a lightning advance in 2025, raising fears of a wider war, and days before the December 4, 2025 White House summit both the DRC military and M23 accused one another of violating the ceasefire.[n] Badlands contributor GhostofBasedPatrickHenry argued that M23 had been dispatched out of Rwanda to seize key chokepoints on behalf of a mineral cartel that lost control of eastern Congolese resources under Executive Order 13818.[n]
democratic-republic-of-the-congo: President Donald Trump hosted DRC President Felix Tshisekedi and Rwandan President Paul Kagame in Washington on December 4, 2025 to sign deals intended to stabilize the region and attract Western mining investment, building on an economic integration compact agreed the previous month and an unimplemented US-brokered peace deal from June.[n] Analysts said American diplomacy had paused escalation in eastern Congo without resolving core issues, and Badlands commentary argued the conflict persists because a cartel that lost control of eastern Congolese minerals under Executive Order 13818 wants them back.[n]
rwanda: Role in the December 2025 Congo peace push

Rwandan President Paul Kagame joined DRC President Felix Tshisekedi at the White House on December 4, 2025 for signings aimed at stabilizing eastern Congo and drawing Western mining investment.[n] The Rwanda-backed M23 rebel group had earlier in the year seized the two largest cities in eastern Congo, and Badlands commentary alleged that the rebels were dispatched out of Rwanda to recapture mineral chokepoints for a cartel displaced by Executive Order 13818.[n]
executive-order-13818: Invoked in the eastern Congo minerals dispute

In December 2025 Badlands contributor GhostofBasedPatrickHenry argued that Executive Order 13818 was the reason a cartel that had once controlled all the minerals of eastern DR Congo lost that control, and that the cartel's desire to regain it explains the deployment of M23 rebels out of Rwanda to seize key chokepoints in the region.[n]
gavin-newsom: At The New York Times' DealBook Summit in early December 2025, actress Halle Berry publicly attacked Newsom for vetoing the Menopause Care Equity Act (AB 432) for the second consecutive year, saying that having overlooked and devalued 'half the population' he 'probably should not be our next president either.'[n] Her remarks reportedly drew gasps from an audience awaiting Newsom's own appearance later that afternoon.[n] Badlands host Ashe in America sided with the veto, arguing the bill was about who pays for menopause care rather than access to it.[n]
ashe-in-america: In the December 5, 2025 Badlands News Brief, Ashe in America argued that Tina Peters was convicted only of misrepresenting who was in her office — a response to Jena Griswold's arbitrary COVID rules — and not of any election-related offense, called Peters' continued imprisonment 'cruel, unusual, and unconstitutional,' and announced a marathon airing of her three-part Peters series on Rumble.[n] She also defended Gavin Newsom's veto of the Menopause Care Equity Act as a dispute over insurance payment rather than health care, and previewed a Why We Vote episode with CannCon and Patrick Byrne on the Venezuelan election fraud story following Emerald Robinson's reporting.[n]
andriy-yermak: Yermak, head of the Office of the President from 2020, stepped down in late 2025 over alleged links to a recently uncovered $100 million money-laundering scheme, formally leaving his post after Western-backed anti-corruption agencies raided his residence as part of the sweeping probe known as Operation Midas; he denied any wrongdoing.[n] His former colleague Yuliya Mendel, Vladimir Zelensky's ex-spokeswoman, said she feared for her life because of him, described him as 'a very dangerous person,' and suggested he retained influence through a network of loyal officials and would 'do absolutely everything' to keep shaping policy behind the scenes or return to power.[n] She further alleged he used smear campaigns, political attacks, and influence over law enforcement to brand critics 'pro-Russian' or 'traitors,' claiming that 'criminal cases are created out of thin air' against perceived threats.[n]
nicolas-maduro: Hugo Carvajal Barrios, the former Venezuelan intelligence chief who served as Director of Military Intelligence under both Hugo Chávez and Maduro, alleged in a ten-page letter from a US federal prison that Maduro's government systematically used drug trafficking, criminal gangs, espionage networks, and even electoral technology to undermine the United States.[n] The letter asserts that Venezuela's ruling elite operates as a 'narco-terrorist organization' with global reach and explicit anti-American intent, and argues that President Donald Trump's policies toward the country are necessary to US national security.[n]
bank-of-england: The Bank of England announced on December 4, 2025 that it was launching a stress test of how the private equity and private credit industries would cope with a financial shock.[n] The system-wide exploratory scenario, due to report in early 2027, focuses on the impact for the British economy as a whole rather than publishing vulnerabilities of individual firms, and Deputy Governor Sarah Breeden said a range of alternative asset managers active in private markets, including major global players, had agreed to participate.[n] Days earlier the bank's half-yearly Financial Stability Report had noted that private markets, though resilient so far, had grown substantially and remained untested against a large economic shock.[n]
andrew-bailey: Ahead of the Bank of England's December 2025 stress test of the private equity and private credit industries, Governor Andrew Bailey had said in October that the collapse of two large US companies — car parts maker First Brands and auto dealership and lender Tricolor — might be a warning of bigger problems to come.[n]
mike-lindell: In December 2025 the MyPillow founder filed state paperwork indicating he might soon launch a campaign for governor of Minnesota in the following year's midterm elections, telling CBS News by phone that he had 'not 100% decided' but had filed in case he moved forward, that he intended to run as a Republican, and that he would address his plans at a press conference the following week.[n] His potential candidacy came as he remained embroiled in multiple legal disputes tied to his claims about the 2020 presidential election, including a federal judge's ruling that he defamed Smartmatic with 'false statements' about its machines and a June jury verdict awarding $2.3 million to a former Dominion Voting Systems employee he had accused of treason.[n]
smartmatic: A federal judge ruled in 2025 that MyPillow founder Mike Lindell had defamed Smartmatic with 'false statements' alleging that the company's machines helped rig the 2020 presidential election, one of several legal disputes still surrounding Lindell as he weighed a run for governor of Minnesota.[n]
dominion-voting-systems: In June 2025 a jury found that Mike Lindell had defamed a former Dominion Voting Systems employee by accusing him of treason, awarding $2.3 million in damages.[n] The verdict was among the legal disputes still hanging over Lindell as he filed paperwork signaling a possible run for governor of Minnesota.[n]
patrick-byrne: In December 2025 Badlands host Ashe in America announced that Byrne would join her and CannCon on Why We Vote to discuss the Venezuelan election fraud story then circulating widely online.[n] She traced the thread from filings in Tina Peters' First Amendment appeal through a Lara Logan interview to reporting by Emerald Robinson, which she said placed Byrne at the center of the matter.[n]
emerald-robinson: Badlands host Ashe in America credited Robinson in December 2025 with advancing the Venezuelan election fraud story, saying that after filings in Tina Peters' First Amendment appeal and a Lara Logan interview, Robinson 'has the ball' and that her reporting placed Patrick Byrne at the center of it all.[n]
canncon: CannCon questioned the framing of the Signalgate report in the December 5, 2025 Badlands News Brief, asking what it would mean if CISA had advised officials to use Signal during the Biden administration about a month before Trump took office, and pointing to Katherine Maher's chairmanship of the Signal Foundation board alongside her NPR role and prior work for the National Democratic Institute, UNICEF, the World Bank, Access Now, the Atlantic Council, and the US State Department Foreign Policy Affairs Board.[n] He also noted that no screenshot had been produced showing how officials in the chat saw Jeffrey Goldberg's name, and was slated to join Ashe in America and Patrick Byrne on Why We Vote to discuss Venezuelan election fraud.[n]
ghostofbasedpatrickhenry: In the December 5, 2025 Badlands News Brief, GhostofBasedPatrickHenry welcomed reports of EU distrust of Washington, writing that he views NATO and the EU — and portions of the United States itself — as the actual bad guys, hoping both institutions collapse from financial mismanagement and public rebuke, and telling Friedrich Merz that Trump would betray him 'because that is the morally righteous thing to do.'[n] He warned that MAGA audiences cheering regime change in Venezuela were endorsing decades-old NeoCon plans and a George Bush agenda item, and pointed to CNN's platforming of former Colombian president Ivan Duque as evidence of a contrived media dialectic.[n] Writing on the eastern Congo conflict, he blamed what he called the Israeli Diamond Cartel — which he said lost control of the region's minerals under Executive Order 13818 and dispatched M23 rebels out of Rwanda to recover them — and, responding to Yuliya Mendel's allegations about Andrey Yermak, launched an extended denunciation of the Republican Party, arguing that MAGA was created to end the GOP.[n]
ivan-duque: Badlands contributor GhostofBasedPatrickHenry cited CNN's platforming of the former Colombian president — whom he described as USAID-backed — as evidence that networks hostile to President Donald Trump nevertheless promote figures supporting the US military campaign to overthrow Nicolás Maduro.[n]
department-of-justice: December 2025 pipe bomb announcement and the Colorado records dispute

The Justice Department scheduled a news conference for December 4, 2025 to formally announce the FBI's first arrest in the nearly five-year January 6 pipe bomb investigation.[n] Separately, Colorado Secretary of State Jena Griswold publicly refused to comply with a department request for Coloradans' sensitive voting information, saying the DOJ 'can take a hike' because it has no legal right to the data.[n]
donald-trump: The Supreme Court agreed on December 4, 2025 to let Texas use a Trump-backed congressional map in the 2026 midterms while litigation continues, a boost to the Republican redistricting campaign to maintain control of Congress.[n] The same day Trump hosted DRC President Felix Tshisekedi and Rwandan President Paul Kagame in Washington to sign deals aimed at stabilizing eastern Congo and attracting Western mining investment, part of a diplomatic push that since January had ranged from the Middle East to Ukraine with mixed results and drew criticism that he should focus on domestic cost-of-living discontent.[n] In a Truth Social post he denounced Colorado Governor Jared Polis as a 'SLEAZEBAG' for keeping Tina Peters jailed and demanded 'FREE TINA!', while his special envoy Steve Witkoff and son-in-law Jared Kushner met Vladimir Putin in Moscow amid European fears of an American betrayal on Ukrainian territory.[n]
why-we-vote: Ashe in America announced that she and CannCon would host Patrick Byrne on Why We Vote to discuss the Venezuelan election fraud story emerging from Tina Peters' First Amendment appeal filings, a Lara Logan interview, and Emerald Robinson's reporting.[n] She also pointed to an earlier episode in which she and Colonel Shawn Smith went through the official narrative on the Peters-commissioned Mesa County reports.[n]
